question: The Holy Quran was revealed to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) over a period of approximately:
detailedExplanation: The Quran was revealed gradually over about 23 years (13 years in Makkah and 10 in Madinah) starting from 610 CE. The first revelation, the opening verses of Surah Al-Alaq, came in the Cave of Hira.
subject: islamic-studies

question: The Holy Quran contains how many surahs?
detailedExplanation: The Holy Quran contains 114 surahs, arranged in 30 juz (paras). Surah Al-Fatiha is the first surah, Al-Baqarah the longest, Al-Kawthar the shortest, and An-Nas is the 114th and last surah.
subject: islamic-studies

question: The first revelation of the Holy Quran was received in which cave?
detailedExplanation: The first revelation (Surah Al-Alaq, verses 1-5) was received by the Prophet (PBUH) in the Cave of Hira on Mount Nur near Makkah in 610 CE, through the Angel Jibrail (AS). The Cave of Thawr sheltered the Prophet during the Hijrah.
subject: islamic-studies

question: Which surah of the Quran contains Ayat-ul-Kursi?
detailedExplanation: Ayat-ul-Kursi (the Verse of the Throne) is verse 255 of Surah Al-Baqarah, the second and longest surah of the Quran. It describes the greatness and attributes of Allah and is widely recited for protection.
subject: islamic-studies

question: Which surah of the Holy Quran is known as the 'Heart of the Quran'?
detailedExplanation: Surah Ya-Sin (the 36th surah) is known as the 'Heart of the Quran' according to a widely cited hadith. Surah Al-Mulk is called the 'Protector' as it intercedes for its reciter, and Surah Al-Ikhlas is equated to one-third of the Quran.
subject: islamic-studies

question: In how many places does the word 'Bismillah-ir-Rahman-ir-Rahim' appear in the Quran?
detailedExplanation: 'Bismillah' appears 114 times in the Quran: at the start of every surah except Surah At-Tawbah (9th surah), and twice in Surah An-Naml (at its opening and again in verse 27:30, in the letter of Prophet Sulaiman to the Queen of Sheba).
subject: islamic-studies

question: Who compiled the Holy Quran in book form during the caliphate of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA)?
detailedExplanation: Zaid bin Thabit (RA), the chief scribe of the Prophet (PBUH), was entrusted by Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) to compile the Quran into a single book (Mushaf) after the Battle of Yamama, in which many Huffaz were martyred. Later, Hazrat Uthman (RA) ordered standardized copies to be sent to provinces.
subject: islamic-studies

question: The Angel who brought revelation (Wahy) to the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was:
detailedExplanation: Jibrail (AS) conveyed the Quranic revelation to the Prophet (PBUH). Israfil (AS) will blow the Trumpet on the Day of Judgment, Mikail (AS) manages provision and rain, and Izrail (AS) takes souls at death.
subject: islamic-studies

question: The Holy Quran mentions the name of which prophet the most number of times?
detailedExplanation: Hazrat Musa (AS) is mentioned about 136 times in the Quran, more than any other prophet. Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) appears about 69 times. Both are regarded as Ulul-Azm (greatest) prophets.
subject: islamic-studies

question: Which kitab (divine book) was revealed to Hazrat Dawood (AS)?
detailedExplanation: The Zabur (Psalms) was revealed to Hazrat Dawood (AS). The Taurat (Torah) came to Hazrat Musa (AS), the Injeel (Gospel) to Hazrat Isa (AS), the Suhuf (scrolls) to earlier prophets, and the Quran to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).
subject: islamic-studies

question: Which is the longest surah of the Holy Quran?
detailedExplanation: Surah Al-Baqarah is the longest surah of the Quran with 286 verses. Surah Al-Kawthar is the shortest with just 3 verses. Al-Imran is the third surah and An-Nisa the fourth.
subject: islamic-studies

question: The major collections of Hadith commonly known as 'Sihah Sittah' are how many in number?
detailedExplanation: The 'Sihah Sittah' (six authentic books) of Hadith are: Sahih Bukhari, Sahih Muslim, Sunan Abu Dawood, Jami Tirmizi, Sunan Nisai and Sunan Ibn Majah. Sahih Bukhari, compiled by Imam Bukhari, is regarded as the most authentic book after the Quran.
subject: islamic-studies

question: Who compiled Sahih Bukhari, the most authentic book of Ahadith?
detailedExplanation: Imam Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Bukhari (810-870 CE) compiled Sahih Bukhari, selecting about 7,275 hadith (including repetitions) from over 600,000 narrations. He was born in Bukhara (Uzbekistan) and died in Samarkand.
subject: islamic-studies

question: What does the term 'Sahih' mean in Hadith terminology?
detailedExplanation: In Hadith sciences, 'Sahih' means authentic - a hadith whose chain of narrators is unbroken, with reliable narrators and no hidden defects. 'Hasan' means good, 'Da'if' means weak, and 'Mawdu' means fabricated.
subject: islamic-studies

question: The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was born in which year?
detailedExplanation: The Prophet (PBUH) was born on 12 Rabi-ul-Awwal, 571 CE in Makkah, in the year known as 'Am-ul-Fil' (Year of the Elephant, when Abraha attacked the Kaaba). His father Abdullah had passed away before his birth.
subject: islamic-studies

question: Who was the mother of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
detailedExplanation: The Prophet's mother was Hazrat Amina bint Wahb, who died when he was about six years old. Hazrat Halima Saadia was his foster mother, Hazrat Khadija was his first wife, and Hazrat Fatima was his daughter.
subject: islamic-studies

question: Hijrat (migration) from Makkah to Madinah took place in which year?
detailedExplanation: The Hijrah took place in 622 CE (September), the 13th year of prophethood. The Prophet (PBUH) migrated with Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) to Yathrib, later named Madinah. The Islamic (Hijri) calendar begins from this event.
subject: islamic-studies

question: Which was the first mosque of Islam, built on arrival in Madinah?
detailedExplanation: Masjid-e-Quba, near Madinah, was the first mosque built in Islam. The Prophet (PBUH) laid its foundation on arriving in Madinah. Masjid-e-Nabawi was built later in Madinah, and Masjid-e-Aqsa in Jerusalem is the first Qibla.
subject: islamic-studies

question: Before the change of Qibla, Muslims used to face which direction in prayer?
detailedExplanation: For about 16-17 months after the Hijrah, Muslims prayed facing Masjid-e-Aqsa in Jerusalem. In 2 AH, the command came (Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 144) to turn towards the Kaaba in Makkah, and the Qibla was changed during Salah.
subject: islamic-studies

question: The Battle of Badr, the first major battle of Islam, took place in which Hijri year?
detailedExplanation: The Battle of Badr was fought on 17 Ramadan, 2 AH (624 CE). About 313 Muslims defeated a much larger Quraysh force. The Quran refers to it as 'Yawm-ul-Furqan' - the day of distinction between truth and falsehood.
subject: islamic-studies

question: In the Battle of Uhud (3 AH), the martyrdom of which uncle of the Prophet (PBUH) occurred?
detailedExplanation: Hazrat Hamza bin Abdul Muttalib (RA), the uncle of the Prophet (PBUH), was martyred in the Battle of Uhud (3 AH) by Wahshi. He was given the title 'Asadullah' (Lion of Allah). The Muslims lost the battle after the archers left their post.
subject: islamic-studies

question: The suggestion of digging a trench around Madinah in the Battle of Khandaq (Ahzab) was given by:
detailedExplanation: In the Battle of the Trench (5 AH), Salman Farsi (RA), who knew Persian defensive techniques, suggested digging a trench around Madinah. The strategy neutralized the allied Quraysh and tribes, and the battle ended without major fighting.
subject: islamic-studies

question: The Conquest of Makkah took place in which year?
detailedExplanation: Makkah was conquered peacefully on 20 Ramadan, 8 AH (630 CE), when the Prophet (PBUH) entered the city with 10,000 men. He forgave the Quraysh, and the idols around the Kaaba were destroyed.
subject: islamic-studies

question: The Farewell Sermon (Khutba Hajjat-ul-Wida) was delivered by the Prophet (PBUH) at:
detailedExplanation: During the Farewell Pilgrimage (10 AH, 632 CE), the Prophet (PBUH) delivered his last sermon on the Mount of Arafat on 9 Dhul-Hijjah. It emphasized equality, human rights, the sanctity of life and property, and adherence to the Quran and Sunnah.
subject: islamic-studies

question: The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) passed away on 12 Rabi-ul-Awwal in which Hijri year?
detailedExplanation: The Prophet (PBUH) passed away on 12 Rabi-ul-Awwal, 11 AH (8 June 632 CE) at the age of 63 in Madinah, and is buried in Masjid-e-Nabawi. Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) was then elected as the first caliph.
subject: islamic-studies

question: Who was the first person to accept Islam from among women?
detailedExplanation: Hazrat Khadija bint Khuwaylid (RA), the wife of the Prophet (PBUH), was the first woman and the first person overall to accept Islam. From men, Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) was the first free man, Hazrat Ali (RA) among youths, and Zaid bin Haritha among slaves.
subject: islamic-studies

question: Who was the first Muazzin (caller of Azaan) of Islam?
detailedExplanation: Hazrat Bilal bin Rabah (RA), an Abyssinian companion, was the first Muazzin of Islam. He was chosen by the Prophet (PBUH) to give the Azaan in Madinah because of his melodious voice.
subject: islamic-studies

question: Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (RA) is also known as:
detailedExplanation: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) was given the title 'Al-Siddiq' (the truthful one) because he affirmed the Prophet's night journey (Isra and Miraj) without hesitation. Umar was 'Al-Farooq' (distinguisher of truth), Uthman 'Zun-Nurain' (possessor of two lights), and Ali 'Haidar' (lion).
subject: islamic-studies

question: Which caliph is called 'Zun-Nurain' (Possessor of Two Lights)?
detailedExplanation: Hazrat Uthman bin Affan (RA) was called 'Zun-Nurain' because he married two daughters of the Prophet (PBUH) - Ruqayyah and Umm Kulthum - at different times. He served as the third caliph (644-656 CE) and arranged standardized copies of the Quran.
subject: islamic-studies

question: The Hijri calendar was formally introduced during the caliphate of:
detailedExplanation: Hazrat Umar (RA) introduced the Islamic (Hijri) calendar in 16 AH, starting from the Hijrah (migration) of the Prophet (PBUH) as year one. He also established the Bait-ul-Mal (public treasury) and founded the cities of Kufa and Basra.
subject: islamic-studies

question: The first caliph of Islam, Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA), died in which year?
detailedExplanation: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) served as caliph for about 2 years and 3 months (11-13 AH, 632-634 CE) and passed away on 22 Jamadi-ul-Akhir 13 AH in Madinah. He fought the Ridda (apostasy) wars and ordered the compilation of the Quran.
subject: islamic-studies

question: The number of obligatory (Fardh) prayers prescribed in a day is:
detailedExplanation: Five daily prayers (Salah) are obligatory: Fajr, Zuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha. They were prescribed during the night journey (Miraj). Jumu'ah (Friday) prayer is obligatory for men in place of Zuhr.
subject: islamic-studies

question: The five daily prayers were made obligatory on the Prophet (PBUH) during:
optionB: The Night of Miraj (Isra wal Miraj)
detailedExplanation: During the Isra and Miraj (27 Rajab), the Prophet (PBUH) journeyed from Makkah to Masjid-e-Aqsa and then to the heavens, where the five daily prayers were prescribed. Initially 50 were commanded, reduced to 5 in merit.
subject: islamic-studies

question: What is the minimum rate of Zakat on wealth in Islam?
detailedExplanation: Zakat is obligatory at the rate of 2.5% (1/40) of qualifying wealth held for a lunar year above the nisab threshold. It is the third pillar of Islam and is to be given to the eight categories of recipients mentioned in Surah At-Tawbah (9:60).
subject: islamic-studies

question: Fasting (Sawm) during Ramadan is obligatory on Muslims and lasts from:
detailedExplanation: Sawm begins at dawn (Fajr) and ends at sunset (Maghrib). The Quran states: 'Eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct from the black thread of night, then complete the fast until night' (Al-Baqarah 2:187).
subject: islamic-studies

question: Laylat-ul-Qadr (the Night of Decree) falls in which nights of Ramadan?
detailedExplanation: Laylat-ul-Qadr is in the last ten nights of Ramadan, most likely the odd nights (21st, 23rd, 25th, 27th or 29th). It is better than a thousand months (Surah Al-Qadr), and the Quran was revealed in it.
subject: islamic-studies

question: Hajj is performed in which Islamic month?
detailedExplanation: Hajj is performed from the 8th to 12th of Dhul-Hijjah, the 12th Islamic month. The Day of Arafat is the 9th, and Eid-ul-Adha is on the 10th of Dhul-Hijjah. Hajj is obligatory once in a lifetime for those who are physically and financially able.
subject: islamic-studies

question: The central rite of Hajj, standing on the plain of Arafat, is performed on:
detailedExplanation: Wuquf (standing) at Arafat on 9 Dhul-Hijjah is the most important rite of Hajj - the Prophet (PBUH) said: 'Hajj is Arafat.' Pilgrims move from Mina to Arafat on 8th and 9th, and the Farewell Sermon was also delivered on this day.
subject: islamic-studies

question: The two hills between which pilgrims perform Saee during Hajj and Umrah are:
detailedExplanation: Saee - walking seven times between Safa and Marwa - commemorates Hazrat Hajra's search for water for her son Ismail (AS), from which the Zamzam well sprang. It is a wajib rite of Hajj and Umrah.
subject: islamic-studies

question: The Holy Quran says belief in how many articles of faith (Iman-e-Mufassal) is required of a Muslim?
detailedExplanation: Iman-e-Mufassal has seven articles: belief in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Day of Judgment, divine decree (good and bad), and life after death. Iman-e-Mujmal summarizes belief in Allah and His attributes.
subject: islamic-studies

question: The Umayyad dynasty, the first hereditary caliphate, was founded by:
detailedExplanation: The Umayyad dynasty was founded by Hazrat Muawiya bin Abu Sufyan (RA) in 661 CE, with Damascus as its capital. It lasted until 750 CE when the Abbasids took over after the Battle of Zab. Abdul Malik bin Marwan built the Dome of the Rock.
subject: islamic-studies

question: The Abbasid caliphate built its capital at which city?
detailedExplanation: The Abbasids moved the capital to Baghdad, founded by Caliph Al-Mansur in 762 CE. Baghdad became the centre of the Islamic Golden Age under Harun-ur-Rashid and Al-Mamun's House of Wisdom. The Mongols sacked it in 1258.
subject: islamic-studies

question: Which Muslim general conquered Spain (Andalusia) in 711 CE?
detailedExplanation: Tariq bin Ziyad led the Muslim conquest of Iberia in 711 CE; Gibraltar (Jabal Tariq) is named after him. Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh (712 CE), Khalid bin Waleed was the great general of the Rashidun era, and Saladin liberated Jerusalem in 1187.
subject: islamic-studies

question: The Ottoman Caliphate was formally abolished in which year?
detailedExplanation: The Ottoman Caliphate was abolished on 3 March 1924 by Mustafa Kemal Ataturk's Turkish Republic. The last caliph was Abdul Majid II. The Khilafat Movement in the subcontinent had been launched to protect it after World War I.
subject: islamic-studies

question: Ibn Sina (Avicenna), one of the greatest Muslim scientists, is famous for his work in:
detailedExplanation: Ibn Sina (980-1037) is known as the 'Prince of Physicians' for his medical encyclopedia 'Al-Qanun fi al-Tibb' (Canon of Medicine), used in European universities for centuries. Al-Khwarizmi contributed to algebra, and Ibn al-Haytham to optics.
subject: islamic-studies
